title.en: A kind stag and a hillock of grass

text.en: An old stag lives in a lush forest and is loved by all the animals. When he falls ill and rests on his hillock of tender grass, his visitors eat the grass until none is left for him. This Panchatantra story teaches us to use nature's resources wisely. In this chapter you will read the story, learn descriptive words and adverbs of manner, write about a friend and think about sharing.

In a lush forest lived an old stag who was known for his kindness. Each day he warmly greeted his fellow animals and birds. Although the forest had plenty of food, the stag liked to stay on a small hillock covered with soft, tender grass. Every day he came down to meet his friends, and all the animals and birds loved him.
One day the stag fell ill and struggled to reach the hillock. He knew that fresh healthy food and proper rest would help him get well, so he ate the tender grass and rested. He could not go down to greet his friends, and they became worried and came to check on him. The deer, elephant and giraffe wished him a speedy recovery.
Before leaving, the visitors ate some of the fresh green grass on the hillock and said how tender and juicy it was. Word spread, and every animal who came to visit the stag also feasted on the grass. Soon there was hardly any grass left for the stag, and he grew weaker day by day. Greed had made his friends forget the very friend they had come to help.
His friends felt ashamed when they realised their mistake. They decided to find food elsewhere in the forest and not disturb the hillock, and some brought fresh leaves for him. That week it rained well, the grass grew back, and slowly the stag recovered. The lesson of this Panchatantra tale is that nature has enough for everybody, but we need to use its resources wisely.
Lush means green and thick, like a lush forest. Tender means soft and young, like tender grass. A hillock is a small hill. A stag is a male deer. Recovery is getting well again, and a speedy recovery is quick healing. A shaded spot is a cool resting place. Healthy food is wholesome food that nourishes us.
Describing words like lush forest, friendly animals and tender grass give more detail and make writing interesting. An adverb of manner tells how something is done. Warmly greeted tells how the stag greeted. Slowly recovered tells how he recovered. Quietly, cheerfully, carefully, loudly, fast and badly are adverbs of manner. Soon, early and lately tell when, and nearby tells where, so they are not adverbs of manner.
In The Monkeys' Fast, monkeys decide to fast till sunset, but they cannot resist peeling bananas and taking just one bite, so they learn that fasting needs self-control. To write about a best friend use pronouns: she or he, her or his. My best friend is Anu. She is eight years old. Her hobby is drawing. Imagine a bowl of jalebis shared in class. If everyone keeps taking more, some friends get none, so we should share and take only our turn. You can make a thank you card from the old stag to his friends for the leaves and the care.
Now let us think about the story. The old stag was popular because he was kind and greeted every animal and bird warmly each day. He could not go down the hillock because he was ill and too weak to walk, and the green grass on the hillock slowly vanished because every visiting animal ate some of it. At the end, the animals realised their mistake. They felt ashamed, looked for food elsewhere in the forest and brought fresh leaves for their friend. Think and discuss: if each of us thought only about our own needs, the plants around us would soon disappear, so we must share nature and use it wisely. Draw the picture that comes to your mind for lush forest, tender grass and healthy food, and then write a sentence for each.

problem.en: Pick the adverb of manner: The rabbit quickly ate the carrots.

text.en: Ask how the rabbit ate.
It ate quickly.
So quickly is the adverb.

why.en: It ends in -ly, which is common for adverbs of manner.

text.en: Recovery means getting well.
So speedy recovery means quick healing.

why.en: It is a kind wish for someone who is ill.

prompt.en: Tell the story of the old stag and explain its lesson.

requiredIdeas.en: The stag stayed on the hillock with tender grass
He fell ill and the visitors ate the grass
The animals felt ashamed and found food elsewhere
Use nature wisely, there is enough for everyone

commonMisconceptions.en: The stag was angry with the animals
The forest had no other food

points.en: The old stag was kind and loved by all.
The visitors ate the grass and left none for the sick stag.
They found food elsewhere and the grass grew back.
Adverbs of manner tell how something is done.
Nature has enough for everybody if we use it wisely.
